pair_convention.spot_explanation: USD/SGD at 1.26714 means 1 US dollar buys 1.26714 Singapore dollars. A rising quote means the US dollar is strengthening versus the Singapore dollar (pair goes up); a falling quote means the Singapore dollar is strengthening versus the US dollar (pair goes down). All levels, targets and pip calculations in this report are anchored to the payload spot of 1.26714 as of the 2026-09-03 close, two sessions after the 2026-09-01 valuation date.

executive_summary: USD/SGD is quoted at 1.26714 as of the 3 September close in the gated price store, two sessions after the 1 September valuation date, and every level, target and pip calculation in this report is anchored to that figure rather than to a fresher vendor quote. The pair has fallen 1.09% over one month, 1.65% over three, 0.54% over six and 0.68% over twelve — a Singapore dollar that has strengthened steadily rather than sharply, and which now sits at the 12th percentile of its 52-week closing range, 4.31% below a 200-week average that has not been closed above for 81 consecutive weeks. The dominant bilateral narrative is a collision between a Federal Reserve that has become the only G10 central bank expected to raise rates and a Monetary Authority of Singapore that has steepened its S$NEER appreciation slope at two consecutive quarterly reviews, and the crucial asymmetry is that MAS's instrument is the exchange rate itself, so the entire policy contest is expressed directly in this pair rather than transmitted through it. Two bilateral differentials diverge sharply from what either standalone dossier implies: the money-market gap of roughly 222bp is a spread against a currency with no policy rate at all, so it is not a policy differential and cannot be read as one, and the six-month forward discount of 160 points already monetises 2.5% annualised Singapore dollar appreciation against a band slope estimated at only about 1.25% — the market has already paid for more than the instrument has ever delivered. The settled verdict is tactically Bullish at conviction 2 (net score +0.2486) and strategically Bearish at conviction 3 (net score −0.3344), an inversion driven mechanically by the fact that the four-week window contains one gated FOMC with projections and no Singapore decision, while the six-month window contains a compounding band slope, a nineteen-percentage-point current-account differential and a Fed whose own dots make September terminal. Our own caveat, stated plainly rather than buried: the price payload the direction pass never saw shows a pair in a clean sequence of lower highs and lower lows into a 12th-percentile close, which sits uncomfortably beside a tactical long, and readers should size the tactical leg as a carry-supported fade of a downtrend rather than as a trend trade. The strategic call is the better one on structure but the worse one on execution, because the forward curve has already priced most of it — which is why this report's central recommendation is that the pair is the right place to state the view and one of the wrong places to express it.

market_context.valuation_assessment: There is no clean PPP construction for this pair. Expressed as a REER-relative proxy, the Singapore dollar screens roughly 5.97% rich against the dollar, implying a USD/SGD near 1.3428 at real-effective parity against a 1.26714 spot — a number whose inputs are 93 days stale and which carries no mean-reversion signal for a currency whose central bank institutionalises permanent real appreciation. The more informative valuation statement is the pair-level one: at the 12th percentile of its 52-week closing range and 4.31% below its 200-week average, the current level prices a market that expects the managed appreciation to continue and is willing to sit near the strong end of the historical distribution to express it.

From the 28 July close of 1.29237 the pair printed a clean sequence of lower highs (1.29383 on 28 July, 1.28414 on 6 August, 1.27913 on 19 August, 1.27541 on 28 August) and lower lows (1.27075 on 19 August, 1.26817 on 21 August, 1.26584 on 3 September, the lowest print of the window). There has been no gap, spike or volatility event: the pair has simply been sold in small increments, exactly what a managed appreciation regime produces. The post-Jackson-Hole dollar rebound failed to lift this specific pair, corroborated by the Singapore dollar's 120-day correlation with the dollar dropping to -0.94, the most inverse link since May 2024 and the most negative in Asia — meaning USD/SGD is currently the purest available regional expression of the dollar leg with almost no independent quote-leg noise.

bilateral_carry_analysis.carry_assessment: Annualised carry is +222.2bp for a long USD/SGD position, based on the US federal funds midpoint of 3.625% minus SORA at 1.4028% — a money-market spread, not a policy differential, since Singapore has no policy interest rate by construction and MAS targets the S$NEER band. A long position is paid roughly 222bp a year, about 282 pips, 23.5 pips a month, or 1.9 pips a trading day, which against a 39-pip ATR(14) means a month of carry is 0.60 of a single average day's range — real but small enough that a two-day adverse move erases it. The carry-to-vol ratio is null because there is no listed option on this pair and therefore no 3-month implied volatility; measured instead against 60-day realised volatility of 3.05% the ratio would be approximately +0.73, the strongest reading in the Singapore dollar complex, but that is a different, non-comparable statistic and is not reported as the framework's carry-to-vol figure. The carry regime is working and the funding environment supports it: the three-month EUR/USD cross-currency basis is essentially zero, Fed swap-line usage is de minimis at $121 million, and realised volatility in this pair is the lowest in the set — precisely the configuration in which carry accrues rather than being wiped out by gaps. The single most important bilateral observation is that the forward curve prices roughly 2.5% annualised Singapore dollar appreciation at every tenor, which is covered interest parity applied to a money-market gap that exists because MAS runs an exchange-rate policy instead of a rate policy, while MAS's instrument at an estimated slope of about 1.25% a year is capable of delivering only about half of it — the pair has actually fallen just 0.68% over the past twelve months, so the forward market systematically over-predicts Singapore dollar appreciation by a factor of two to three, the single largest structural fact about trading this pair.

factors.weight_adjustment_reason: The money-market differential of about 222bp exceeds the 200bp threshold at which the framework contemplates a boost, and more fundamentally one leg has no policy rate at all: MAS's instrument is the exchange rate, so the entire policy contest between the two economies is expressed directly in this pair rather than transmitted through it. Factor 1 is doing double duty here.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The bilateral differential is unusually awkward to state because Singapore has no policy rate: MAS sets the slope, width and centre of the S$NEER band, and SORA at 1.4028 per cent is a money-market proxy explicitly not a policy instrument. On that proxy the dollar out-yields Singapore by about 222 basis points, the second-widest positive carry the dollar runs against anything in the G10-plus-Singapore set after the franc and the yen. The trajectory over four weeks favours the dollar for a reason that is calendar rather than conceptual: the only gated policy decision inside the window is the FOMC on 2026-09-16, which carries a Summary of Economic Projections and a 57 to 68 per cent implied probability of a 25bp increase to 3.75-4.00 per cent, and there is no Singapore decision in the gated calendar at all. If the hike is delivered the money-market gap widens to roughly 247bp, and because the S$NEER is trade-weighted rather than dollar-pegged the Singapore dollar can keep appreciating against its basket while USD/SGD still rises. The transmission is the forward curve: vendor-quoted points of minus 27.2 at one month and minus 160.0 at six already embed about 2.5 per cent annualised Singapore dollar appreciation against an estimated band slope of only about 1.25 per cent, so anyone short USD/SGD is paying a hurdle that MAS's own instrument has never delivered. The offset, and the reason confidence is not higher, is that roughly two-thirds of the hike is already discounted, so the residual asymmetry on the day sits with a hold rather than a delivery.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the same differential stops widening and starts decaying, and the two legs move in opposite directions. On the dollar side the Committee's own June projections carry a 2026 median of 3.8 per cent and a 2027 median of 3.6 per cent, which on the Fed's own arithmetic makes a September move terminal with a cut behind it; the gated calendar then puts a decision on 2026-10-28 without projections and one on 2026-12-09 with them, and the December Summary of Economic Projections is the specific release at which a terminal hike is either confirmed or converted into a cycle. On the Singapore side the mechanism compounds rather than decays: a band slope of 1.25 to 1.50 per cent a year delivers 60 to 75 basis points of trade-weighted appreciation over six months whether or not anyone believes in it, and MAS has tightened at two consecutive quarterly reviews with core inflation now accelerating into the next one. The differential therefore peaks somewhere in the fourth quarter and narrows thereafter, which points USD/SGD lower. The transmission is covered interest parity working in reverse of the tactical read: as the dollar's front-end advantage stops growing, the forward discount stops being a hurdle and starts being a floor. Confidence is capped at 52 because the timing of the Singapore leg cannot be anchored to a gated date and because a second Fed hike into the 2026-12-09 meeting would reverse the sign of this factor outright.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: This factor is a genuine standoff and the standoff is structural rather than a failure to choose. The inflation differential favours the dollar: US core PCE has been stuck at 3.3 per cent for three months with headline PCE at 3.7 per cent, against MAS core inflation of 2.0 per cent and Singapore headline of 2.2 per cent, so the dollar leg carries the larger absolute inflation problem and the central bank most likely to react to it inside the window. The growth differential runs hard the other way and is not close: Singapore printed 5.9 per cent year on year in the second quarter with unemployment at 2.0 per cent and the Ministry of Trade and Industry lifting its full-year forecast from 2.0-4.0 per cent to 4.5-5.5 per cent, against US growth of 2.1 per cent on the OECD vintage, 1.5 per cent annualised in the second quarter on the BEA second estimate, and payrolls that fell 23,000 in July with average hourly earnings at a five-year low of 3.2 per cent. The transmission asymmetry is what produces the draw: in the US, higher inflation becomes a higher policy rate and therefore more carry, which lifts USD/SGD; in Singapore, higher inflation and a wider output gap become a steeper appreciation path, which lowers it. Both economies are running hot on prices for the same imported-energy reason, and both central banks are being pushed the same way, so the pair gets no clean signal. The asymmetric data sensitivity is that US releases move this pair far harder than Singapore's — payrolls on 2026-09-04 and CPI on 2026-09-11 both land before the FOMC, while Singapore's August CPI on 2026-09-23 has no policy meeting behind it inside the window.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the standoff resolves toward the Singapore dollar, because the two inflation impulses have different half-lives and the growth gap does not close. The US impulse is substantially tariff-driven — an average statutory rate of 11.0 per cent is a one-off level shift that drops out of the year-on-year comparison — and it sits on top of a labour market that is deteriorating rather than tightening, with participation at 61.4 per cent and wage growth at a five-year low. The base dossier itself moves this factor to Neutral over six months for that reason. Singapore's impulse is younger and mechanically renewing: the third-quarter regulated electricity tariff only began passing through in July, lifting electricity and gas 8.7 per cent year on year, the tariff resets quarterly, and MAS's own guidance is that core steps up from July and stays elevated until moderating around mid-2027. Crucially, in Singapore that inflation is not a drag on the currency but its driver, because the exchange rate is the instrument. The growth differential also persists at an extreme: even with semiconductor output growth decelerating from 37.0 per cent in May to 8.0 per cent in July, the level of activity supports a widening positive output gap that MAS has explicitly acknowledged. The transmission is therefore that the same six months in which the US inflation impulse fades are the six months in which Singapore's forces a steeper band, and both point USD/SGD lower. The qualification, and the reason confidence is 55 rather than higher, is that Singapore's export strength has narrowed to three product lines while pharmaceuticals fell 56.7 per cent, so the growth leg is more fragile than the headline suggests.

factors.horizon_split: The stance moves from Neutral to Bearish because the tactical horizon is decided by which central bank has a meeting and the strategic horizon by which inflation impulse lasts. tactical.bilateral_analysis: USD/SGD belongs firmly in the framework's low risk-sensitivity bucket, and the reason is that both legs are haven currencies operating at different scales. The dollar is the global haven and benefits from any broad volatility spike; the Singapore dollar is Asia's haven, AAA-rated with a 16.7 per cent-of-GDP current-account surplus and roughly 428 billion dollars of official reserves, and it gains specifically when stress is regional. In a broad risk-off the dollar wins the pair even while the Singapore dollar outperforms every Asian peer, which is the dollar-smile asymmetry stated plainly. The current environment gives neither leg its bid: the VIX closed at 14.43 on 2026-08-28 after falling 6.23 points on the month, US investment-grade spreads are 79bp and high yield 260bp near post-crisis tights, and the Straits Times Index set an all-time high in August. Benign conditions are mildly dollar-negative through the carry-outflow channel and mildly Singapore-dollar-positive through the trade and electronics channel, and those two effects are of similar small size. The cross-asset variable that actually matters most for this pair is USD/CNH at 6.7214, firm and stable, given the normal-range 0.4 to 0.6 correlation between USD/SGD and USD/CNH — and it is currently signalling nothing. The distribution is skewed, though: from a 14.43 VIX the tail is overwhelmingly higher, and every point of that skew is USD/SGD-positive, which is a reason to prefer Neutral over Bearish.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the risk channel carries tails rather than a trend, and the tails point in opposite directions for this pair with roughly equal weight. The bullish USD/SGD tail is a broad global risk-off from spreads that have no room to tighten — 79bp investment grade and 260bp high yield leave no cushion — in which the dollar dominates as the world's haven and USD/SGD rises regardless of the Singapore dollar outperforming its region. The bearish USD/SGD tail is a synchronised expansion that keeps capital rotating into Asian growth and into Singapore's asset-management franchise, which MAS is actively institutionalising through its August package of a fund tax exemption from year of assessment 2027 and a new Hedge Fund Investment Programme framed explicitly against Hong Kong. There is a third possibility that is genuinely ambiguous: a China- or Taiwan-specific stress event drives capital into Singapore while simultaneously driving the dollar higher, so the pair's direction depends on which flow is larger and there is no way to know in advance. Notably, the broad trade-weighted dollar fell 1.69 per cent on the month while the G10-only basket fell only 0.37 per cent, which says the dollar has been losing ground to emerging markets rather than to peers — a configuration that is mildly bearish USD/SGD but not enough to call the factor. Neutral at low confidence is the honest output.

factors.horizon_split: Both horizons are Neutral and the two-point confidence gap reflects composition, not direction. Tactically the reading is anchored on observable levels — a 14.43 VIX, 79bp spreads, a stable USD/CNH — while strategically it depends on which of three unrelated regime shifts arrives first, two of which lift the pair and one of which lowers it. The mechanism is identical on both: a global haven on one side and a regional haven on the other.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the bilateral flow picture splits into two structural trends that pull the pair in opposite directions and are of comparable size. Against the dollar, the reserve-manager channel is one-way and slow: the dollar's share of allocated global reserves was 57.13 per cent in the first quarter of 2026, up from a 56.42 per cent fourth quarter that was the first sub-57 reading since 1995 but still roughly fifteen points below the 2001 peak, and speculative length enters the window from a multi-year high so the distribution of change is skewed toward reduction. For the Singapore dollar, structural inflows are persistent rather than cyclical — corporate treasury and regional headquarters relocation, family-office formation, and now an explicit MAS policy push into asset management — and they must be converted into Singapore dollars for operating purposes. Both of those point USD/SGD lower. Working the other way is the bounded nature of the quote leg's crowding: if MAS holds its slope, the estimated 1.7 per cent band deviation unwinds toward the midpoint, a move of about 1.5 per cent on the trade-weighted index and less on this pair, and there is no leveraged futures book to squeeze so the unwind would be orderly rather than violent. The net is Neutral, and the weight of 0.02 reflects that this factor is better used to bound the distribution than to point it.

Tactically the two legs' crowding offsets with a small tilt from the quote leg's thin band headroom; strategically two persistent structural trends — de-dollarisation at the margin and Singapore's inflow franchise — both point the pair lower but neither is fast enough to be a driver over six months. tactical.bilateral_analysis: Over four weeks the external accounts are inert but the terms of trade are not, and the terms-of-trade differential currently favours the dollar. Singapore is a net crude importer and refined-product exporter whose largest single product deficit in 2025 was mineral fuels at minus 24.7 billion dollars; its terms-of-trade index fell to 97.84 in July from 98.66 and its domestic supply price index is running at plus 33.4 per cent year on year, the clearest single measure of an import-cost shock anywhere in the eleven-currency set. The United States, by contrast, is now a net energy exporter, so the same Brent price that is squeezing Singapore is a mild terms-of-trade positive for the base leg. With Brent having rebounded to roughly 93 dollars by 2026-08-31 on escalating US-Iran hostilities and the Strait of Hormuz severely constrained since late February, the near-term commodity netting is USD/SGD-positive. The bilateral trade relationship itself is not a driver: IMF Direction of Trade Statistics show US exports to Singapore of 46.0 billion dollars against imports of 43.2 billion in 2024, a small US surplus of 2.8 billion, close to balanced and tiny relative to either economy's total flows. The offsetting facts are large but slow — Singapore runs the largest current-account surplus in the set at 16.7 per cent of GDP against a US deficit of 2.9 per cent — and a quarterly current-account release does not move a currency in September. Hence a low-confidence Bullish read at a 0.06 weight.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: At a 0.16 strategic weight this becomes the second-largest factor and it is decisively bearish USD/SGD, because over quarters the cumulative balance-of-payments flow dominates the price of imports. The differential is close to the widest available anywhere in the G10-plus-Singapore set: a Singapore current-account surplus of 16.7 per cent of GDP against a US deficit of 2.9 per cent that is widening, and a Singapore net creditor position against a US net international investment position of minus 21.27 trillion dollars. The composition change on the base leg matters as much as the level: the US primary income balance flipped from surplus to deficit in the first quarter of 2026, which attacks the specific mechanism — earning more on foreign assets than is paid on foreign liabilities — that has allowed a deeply negative investment position to coexist with a stable currency for two decades. On the quote leg the surplus is absorbed partly through reserve accumulation of 33.8 billion Singapore dollars over twelve months and partly through the persistent real appreciation that the S$NEER band institutionalises, precisely the transmission channel this pair trades. The commodity netting runs the other way and is the main offset, since Brent up roughly 37 per cent year on year is a genuine drag on the quote leg — but a six-month oil drag does not outrun a structural surplus of that scale. The qualification is Singapore's export concentration: three product lines carry a 24.2 per cent headline while pharmaceuticals fell 56.7 per cent, and 22.0 per cent of goods exports go to Greater China into a tariff-truce expiry on 2026-11-10.

factors.horizon_split: The stance flips from Bullish to Bearish because the weight and the clock both change. At a 0.06 tactical weight the surplus is a slow constant with no four-week information content, so the fast-moving oil shock decides the sign and it favours the dollar. At a 0.16 strategic weight the cumulative flow becomes the dominant channel: nearly twenty percentage points of GDP of annual current-account differential, absorbed through reserve accumulation and real appreciation, outruns a six-month energy drag.

net_commodity_exposure.base_commodity_profile: The United States is now a net energy exporter, so rising crude is a mild terms-of-trade positive and a clear inflation positive reinforcing the hawkish policy channel. Brent fell from $100.31 to $88.24 over the month before rebounding to roughly $93; Henry Hub at $2.70 is unremarkable. Gold at $4,448.80 is rallying alongside a firm dollar, reading as a debasement hedge rather than a dollar-alternative trade.
net_commodity_exposure.quote_commodity_profile: Singapore is a net crude importer and refined-product exporter with a mineral-fuels trade deficit of -$24.7bn in 2025 and processed petroleum oils as its second-largest export at $51.5bn. Rising crude and rising LNG both hit it directly: the domestic supply price index at +33.4% year on year and the terms-of-trade index at 97.84 are the observable damage.
net_commodity_exposure.net_effect_calculation: Apply the framework rules leg by leg. Oil up: the United States as a net energy exporter takes a mild positive (+); Singapore is explicitly (−) on the rule set, amplified by a $24.7bn mineral-fuels deficit. Netting (+) against (−) gives base stronger than quote, so the pair RISES — oil up is bullish USD/SGD. LNG up compounds it in the same direction, since JKM up is −−SGD and neutral-to-positive for a US exporter. Gold up is broadly neutral for both legs. The complication is that Singapore's oil shock is exactly what forces MAS to steepen the appreciation band — MAS cited surging imported energy prices driven by the Middle East crisis and used a stronger currency as a buffer against imported inflation — so the terms-of-trade hit and the policy response point opposite ways, with the ToT effect faster and the policy effect larger and slower. That interaction is why this factor is Bullish tactically and Bearish strategically while Factor 1 does the reverse.
net_commodity_exposure.scenario_oil_up_10pct: Brent from roughly $93 to about $102. Singapore's import bill and domestic supply prices deteriorate immediately while the US takes a mild export gain, so USD/SGD rises on a four-week view — perhaps 30 to 50 pips given the pair's 3.05% realised volatility and 39-pip ATR. Over three months the sign becomes ambiguous, because a Brent above $100 would make a further MAS slope increase close to a certainty.
net_commodity_exposure.scenario_oil_down_10pct: Brent from roughly $93 to about $84. Singapore's terms of trade improve and the domestic supply price index decelerates (quote-positive), but it simultaneously removes the imported-inflation impulse that justifies a steeper band (quote-negative through the policy channel). Net effect close to neutral for the pair, with a mild bearish USD/SGD tilt tactically and a mild bullish one strategically.
net_commodity_exposure.dominant_commodity_driver: Crude oil, specifically the Brent price transmitted through Singapore's quarterly regulated electricity tariff and its mineral-fuels deficit. Nothing else in the commodity complex splits these two legs as cleanly.

factors.weight_adjustment_reason: For most pairs guidance is a signal about a future rate decision; for USD/SGD one central bank's guidance IS its exchange-rate setting, because MAS communicates the slope of the band rather than a rate path. Guidance divergence therefore transmits into this pair more directly than into any other in the set.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: Both central banks are guiding hawkish, so the bilateral question is entirely about sequencing and refresh, and over four weeks that favours the dollar. On the base leg the guidance is live and unusually pointed: the June Summary of Economic Projections raised the 2026 median to 3.8 per cent from 3.4 per cent, the July meeting produced a 9-3 hold in which all three dissenters wanted a hike — the first three-dissent meeting with a unified direction since September 2016 — and Chair Warsh used the 28 August Jackson Hole keynote to say the better summer inflation readings do not tell him underlying trends have meaningfully improved, quoting headline PCE at 3.7 per cent and 4.1 per cent annualised over six months. The market repriced immediately and still sits below the dots, an unusual configuration in which the central bank is more hawkish than the curve. On the quote leg the guidance is equally hawkish in substance — MAS steepened the band at two consecutive reviews and its Managing Director said on 28 July that the stronger appreciation will lean more effectively against incoming inflationary pressures — but it is static: there has been no MAS exchange-rate communication of any kind since 28 July, and the gated calendar carries no SGD decision at all, so nothing refreshes it inside the window. The transmission is therefore asymmetric by calendar: the base leg gets a dated communication event with projections attached on 2026-09-16 and the quote leg gets silence. Credibility is high on both sides; the differential is one of timing.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the guidance differential reverses, and it reverses for a mechanical reason. The Fed's own projections make the September move terminal — a 2026 median of 3.8 per cent followed by a 2027 median of 3.6 per cent — so the base leg's guidance, however hawkish today, is guidance toward a plateau and then an easing. The gated calendar puts the test on 2026-12-09, the meeting with a fresh Summary of Economic Projections at which the 2027 median is either held at 3.6 per cent, confirming a terminal hike, or lifted, converting it into a cycle. MAS's guidance points the other way and compounds: it tightened in April before the shock appeared in the data and again in July while the most recent core print had eased to 1.6 per cent, a central bank acting on its own projection twice in a row, and every print since has validated that projection — core to 2.0 per cent, headline to 2.2 per cent, the domestic supply price index at plus 33.4 per cent, growth revised up to 4.5-5.5 per cent and the output gap now expected to widen rather than narrow. The transmission into the pair is unusually direct because MAS's communication is its instrument: a statement containing 'increase the rate of appreciation' rather than 'maintain the prevailing rate of appreciation' moves the band and therefore the pair, without any intervening rate decision. Credibility favours the quote leg too — a regime running since 1981 with no successful market challenge, against a Fed whose main strategic risk is an institutional question about political pressure rather than an analytical one.

We think the second reading is the weaker one given a revealed reaction function that has front-run its own data twice, and that disagreement is the cleanest strategic argument for a lower USD/SGD.

factors.horizon_split: The stance inverts on sequencing. Tactically the base leg has a dated, projection-bearing communication event on 2026-09-16 and the quote leg has had no exchange-rate communication since 28 July and nothing scheduled on the gated file, so hawkish-but-static loses to hawkish-and-refreshing. Strategically the Fed's own dots make its hawkishness terminal while MAS's band slope compounds and its review cycle delivers another decision point, so the same two hawkish central banks produce opposite pair signals.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The four-week calendar is asymmetric and both of its live items point the same way for this pair. The dominant event is the gated FOMC decision on 2026-09-16 with a Summary of Economic Projections attached, a genuine binary at 57-68 per cent for a hike whose delivery mechanically widens the money-market gap to about 247bp; the quote leg has no scheduled decision on the gated file to answer it. The second item is energy geopolitics, and here the asymmetry is structural rather than calendar-driven: shipping through the Strait of Hormuz has been severely constrained since late February on MAS's own account, the 60-day US-Iran memorandum expired on 17 August with no successor and no talks scheduled, and Brent rebounded toward 93 dollars on 2026-08-31. Escalation helps the base leg twice over — safe-haven demand plus a terms-of-trade gain for a net energy exporter — and hurts the quote leg twice over, through an import bill already visible in a plus 33.4 per cent domestic supply price index and through Singapore's position as the most trade-dependent large economy in the set. Trade policy adds a third, smaller tilt in the same direction: a 12.5 per cent US tariff imposed on 24 July affects roughly 9.5 billion Singapore dollars of exports, about a third of shipments to the United States. The analytical handicap is that event pricing cannot be tested, because this pair has no options market at all.

Hormuz escalation is priced nowhere in credit or equity volatility and is the tail that hits the quote leg hardest, which is why the four-week calendar tilts the pair higher.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: The one-to-six-month calendar is unusually dense with dated binaries and Singapore's extreme trade openness means the quote leg is exposed to nearly all of them, which is what keeps this factor bullish USD/SGD even at low confidence. The cluster runs: US midterm elections on 2026-11-03, the US-China tariff truce expiry on 2026-11-10 with China's reciprocal truce on 2026-11-19 and the tariff-exclusion process on 2026-12-31, Taiwan's local elections on 2026-11-28, and the US government funding cliff on 2026-12-11. Singapore sends 22.0 per cent of its goods exports to Greater China and 9.6 per cent to the United States, so a truce failure hits both ends of its entrepot function simultaneously, and total merchandise trade running at plus 38.6 per cent year on year is the flow that gets disrupted. Its export boom is now concentrated in integrated circuits and disk media, with Taiwan among its largest destinations, which makes the Taiwan date a specific rather than generic exposure. The base leg's own event risk is real but genuinely two-sided: the midterms cut both ways through the fiscal and growth channels, and the tariff legal question could resolve either inflationary or disinflationary. The mechanism that makes the net sign positive for the pair is the dollar smile — the same regional shock that would drive capital into Singapore against its Asian peers would drive the dollar higher against everything, so the quote leg's haven status does not protect it in this specific pair.

The bilateral asymmetry is that the quote leg's real economy is more exposed while the base leg's currency benefits from the same shock.

factors.horizon_split: Both horizons are Bullish and the two-point confidence gap reflects a change in composition rather than direction. Tactically the risk is one largely-priced monetary binary plus an unpriced energy tail, both pointing the pair higher. Strategically it fragments across five dated political and trade events, all of which run through Singapore's trade channel, partly offset by the base leg's own genuinely two-sided midterm and tariff questions.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The fiscal differential in this pair is the widest of any factor in the analysis and it points one way, but over four weeks it is transmitting backwards, which is why the stance is Bearish at the lowest confidence in this analysis. The quote leg is rated Aaa by Moody's and AAA by S&P, runs a projected FY2026 surplus of about 1.0 per cent of GDP, and is a substantial net creditor: the widely misread 171.3 per cent gross debt figure is issued for investment under the Government Securities Act rather than to fund deficits, and GIC plus Temasek stand near 1.34 trillion dollars against a GDP of roughly 560 billion. The base leg is rated Aa1 and AA+, has borrowed 1.8 trillion dollars over the first ten months of fiscal 2026 with a run-rate above 2 trillion, carries debt held by the public at 101 per cent of GDP, and faces projected interest costs of 1,039 billion dollars that would exceed the post-war high of 3.2 per cent of GDP. On arithmetic alone this is a decisive quote-leg win. The tactical problem is the transmission: the bond market is charging for the US position at the long end, with the 30-year at 5.22 per cent and a 30-year TIPS auction clearing 50bp higher than the prior, and on 2026-09-01 a global bond rout lifted yields, pushed gold to a ten-day low and left the dollar firm. In the current regime a widening US deficit expressed through higher long yields is dollar-supportive, not dollar-destructive, so the factor's sign is right and its short-run mechanism is inverted. Neither sovereign has a rating catalyst inside the window.

tactical.what_is_priced: US fiscal risk is priced almost entirely in the long end and not at all in the currency, and Singapore's sovereign strength is priced fully and correctly. Over four weeks higher US long yields are dollar-supportive, so the fiscal channel is temporarily working against its own arithmetic.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the fiscal differential becomes a materially larger drag on the pair, and confidence rises twenty-two points, because the mechanism that currently neutralises it is the same mechanism that eventually breaks it. US interest costs compound automatically as low-coupon debt rolls into a 4.5 to 5.2 per cent curve, and there is a specific interaction with Factor 1 that the market does not price: a hike on 2026-09-16 raises the front-end rollover cost directly, so the policy action that supports the dollar tactically enlarges the fiscal burden that undermines it strategically. On the quote leg the sovereign balance sheet is not merely strong, it is the enabling condition for the whole exchange-rate regime — a country with a weak external balance sheet cannot credibly commit to persistent real appreciation because it cannot fund the reserve accumulation the policy requires, and Singapore's reserves rising 33.8 billion Singapore dollars year on year to 549.3 billion is exactly that funding. Singapore is also deploying fiscal capacity offensively, with a proposed fund tax exemption from year of assessment 2027 and a Hedge Fund Investment Programme designed to defend its asset-management franchise, a fiscal cost incurred to protect a capital-inflow channel and therefore quote-currency-positive. The offset is genuine: S&P's June affirmation of the US at AA+ explicitly cited credible, effective monetary policy execution, and a September hike reinforces precisely that credibility. The transmission to watch is auction reception rather than gradual drift.

strategic.what_is_priced: The market prices the US fiscal position as a term-premium problem confined to the long end and not as a currency problem, and prices Singapore's AAA status as a given with no instrument in which to differentiate. The unpriced element is the interaction: a hike that supports the dollar while raising the rollover cost of a $40 trillion debt stock.

factors.horizon_split: The stance is Bearish on both horizons but confidence rises from 40 to 62, and the reason is mechanical. Tactically the channel is inverted — the 2026-09-01 bond rout lifted US yields and the dollar together, so a deteriorating deficit currently reads as dollar-supportive. Strategically that inversion cannot persist: interest costs compound, a hike at the gated 2026-09-16 decision accelerates the rollover repricing, and the quote leg's balance sheet is the precondition for the very band that drags the pair lower.

factors.weight_adjustment_reason: Half of this factor's normal content does not exist for this pair: there is no listed USD/SGD option anywhere, so implied volatility, the term structure, the variance risk premium, the risk reversal and any event premium are permanently absent rather than merely unobtained.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: This is the one factor where the pair's own trading behaviour is the legitimate subject, and the honest reading is Neutral because the informative half of it is missing by construction. There is no listed USD/SGD option on any exchange — no SGD options in any CME product family, no SGD entry in the CVOL index family, no options on the SGX USD/SGD futures root — and the direction payload states the same and instructs that no estimate be substituted. Implied volatility, the one-year implied percentile, the variance risk premium, the vol term structure and the 25-delta risk reversal are therefore all null, and the standard test of whether the 2026-09-16 FOMC is adequately hedged in this pair cannot be run at all. What is observable is realised volatility, and it is among the lowest in the eleven-currency set: 3.47 per cent over twenty days against 3.05 per cent over sixty, which is what a managed band produces. The one genuine signal in that pair of numbers is that the short window has moved above the long one, which in a managed float is one of the few reliable tells that the trade-weighted index is approaching a band edge or that a policy review is drawing near. Both happen to be true. Adding the price-payload structure that the direction pass could not see: spot at 1.26714 sits below the 50-day (1.28385), 100-day (1.28190) and 200-day (1.28077) simple averages while the averages themselves remain stacked bullishly, and 4.31% below a 200-week average at 1.32176 that has been unbroken to the downside for 81 weeks. Event Risk adds +0.0260 because Hormuz escalation is doubly positive for the pair, helping a net energy exporter on terms of trade and haven demand while hitting a net crude importer whose domestic supply price index is already at +33.4 per cent. consensus_divergence.bank_consensus_forecast: UBS has maintained USD/SGD forecasts at 1.26 by September 2026, 1.25 by December 2026 and 1.24 by March 2027, implying further Singapore dollar gains. MUFG's 3 August 2026 table shows 1.2900 for Q3 and Q4 2026, 1.2850 for Q1 2027 and 1.2700 for Q2 — a weaker Singapore dollar than spot for three consecutive quarters. DBS projects a 1.25-1.30 range January to September 2026, and independent commentary places the pair around S$1.25-1.30.
consensus_divergence.bank_consensus_forecast_source: UBS; MUFG (published table dated 2026-08-03, carried via the quote dossier); DBS
consensus_divergence.our_strategic_view: Bearish to 1.2480 by end-February 2027 over six months
consensus_divergence.divergence_direction: Tactically above UBS's 1.26 September path; strategically stronger Singapore dollar than MUFG's 1.2850 Q1 path and close to UBS's 1.24 March 2027 target
consensus_divergence.divergence_magnitude: +180 pips above UBS's tactical 1.26 September number; -320 pips versus MUFG's 1.2850 Q1 2027 path; roughly -80 pips versus UBS's 1.24 March 2027 target on a like-for-like basis
consensus_divergence.why_we_differ: Against MUFG the disagreement is about whether MAS's instrument keeps working: a forecast of a weaker Singapore dollar than spot for three consecutive quarters is hard to reconcile with an appreciating trade-weighted band at all, since it implies either that MAS abandons the slope after two consecutive tightenings or that the dollar rallies enough to overwhelm it, and neither is our base case given a June dot plot whose 2027 median of 3.6% makes the September hike terminal. Against UBS the disagreement is about the next four weeks rather than the next six months: UBS's 1.26 for September implies the pair keeps grinding through the FOMC, and we think a 222bp carry plus a projection-bearing Fed meeting with no Singapore decision to answer it produces at least a temporary bounce. We also weigh External Balance at 0.16 rather than treating a nineteen-percentage-point current-account differential as permanent background, and Guidance at 0.15 because for this pair a central bank statement is the policy setting.
consensus_divergence.payoff_if_right: Tactically, roughly +107 pips of base-case move plus about +23.5 pips of monthly carry, against a consensus positioned for continuation lower. Strategically, USD/SGD at 1.2480 by end-February against MUFG's implied 1.2850 — a 370-pip gap — with the cleanest capture in the low-carry Singapore dollar crosses rather than in this pair, where the forward already prices 1.26% of the 1.51% we expect.
consensus_divergence.risk_if_wrong: The tactical view fails if the Fed holds on 16 September against 57-68% priced, which would strand a still-positive dollar book and take the pair through 1.25883 to the downside case. The strategic view fails in two identifiable ways: MAS holds its slope in October, unwinding the estimated 1.7% band deviation toward the midpoint and vindicating MUFG; or the Fed delivers a second hike into 9 December, widening the money-market gap toward 297bp, enough to overwhelm the band slope in the primary pair. Both failure modes are bounded rather than open-ended, because the band truncates the distribution on both sides.

cross_horizon_consistency.explanation: The horizons genuinely oppose each other and the opposition is mechanical rather than a hedge. Over four weeks the pair is driven by which central bank has a meeting and how much carry the dollar pays: the gated calendar puts an FOMC with projections on 16 September and carries no SGD decision at all, and the dollar earns about 222bp for waiting. Over one to six months it is driven by which policy path compounds and which economy has the stronger balance sheet: the Fed's own dots make September terminal with a cut behind it, while MAS's band slope delivers 60 to 75bp of trade-weighted appreciation mechanically, on top of a nineteen-percentage-point current-account differential and a sovereign gap between AAA and Aa1. Three factors change sign between horizons — Policy and Rates, Guidance, and External Balance — and each change has a specific, dated reason rather than a change of mood.
cross_horizon_consistency.inflection_point: The gated 16 September FOMC is the first inflection, because the Summary of Economic Projections released alongside it resolves the tactical event and sets the strategic path in the same release: if the 2027 median holds at 3.6%, the strategic Bearish reading is confirmed. The second and larger inflection is the quote leg's autumn policy review, which the quote dossier places in mid-October alongside the Macroeconomic Review and the Q3 advance GDP estimate — not in the gated calendar, carried as dossier-sourced and unverified. The general quarterly cadence (January, April, July, October reviews) is independently confirmed, but the specific date is not.
cross_horizon_consistency.trading_implication: Treat the tactical long as a trade with an expiry rather than the opening leg of a position, and do not size it as though the strategic view will eventually agree with it. The tactical view is carry-positive and can be held in spot or a rolled forward at +23.5 pips a month, whereas the strategic view is carry-negative and starts 160 points behind at six months. No options market exists in this pair at any tenor, so neither view can be given convexity. The strategic view is better expressed in low-carry Singapore dollar crosses than in the primary pair, where the forward has already monetised most of the expected move; the primary pair is where the view should be stated and monitored, using the 1.25883 and 1.28840 boundaries as the two decision levels.

catalysts.event: US August non-farm payrolls, unemployment rate and average hourly earnings
catalysts.rationale: The largest data risk before the gated FOMC. Consensus is +58,000 after July's -23,000, with average hourly earnings at a five-year low of 3.2%. A second consecutive contraction would make a hike twelve days later very hard to defend, removing the tactical carry-widening argument that supplies most of the positive score; a firm print entrenches it. The quote leg has no scheduled release to answer either outcome, so the pair's reaction is a pure base-leg function.

catalysts.event: US August CPI, University of Michigan preliminary, monthly federal budget balance
catalysts.rationale: The last US inflation print before the FOMC, against a July base of 3.4% headline and 2.5% core. The unusual configuration is that core CPI sits 80bp below core PCE at 3.3%, an inversion of the normal sign, so a soft core CPI reading is less dovish for this pair than it looks — the Fed targets PCE and the Chair quoted headline PCE at Jackson Hole. Transmission runs entirely through the base leg's rate path and therefore the carry.

catalysts.event: Federal Reserve FOMC decision with Summary of Economic Projections (gated)
catalysts.rationale: The dominant dated event in the tactical window and the only gated decision for either currency inside it. A 25bp hike to 3.75-4.00% is carried at 57-68% in futures against roughly 48-55% in prediction markets, and delivery widens the money-market gap from about 222bp to 247bp. The projections released alongside also reset the strategic path, since the 2027 median of 3.6% is what currently makes the move terminal — so this single release resolves the tactical trade and sets the strategic one.

catalysts.event: Singapore August merchandise trade and non-oil domestic exports
catalysts.rationale: July NODX rose 24.2% year on year with electronics at +112% and non-electronics contracting 2.3%. The tell is the split rather than the headline: electronics has exceeded +90% for three months on base effects that begin fading from Q4, while pharmaceuticals fell 56.7%. A weak print undermines the growth case behind a steeper appreciation band and is therefore bullish USD/SGD; a strong one reinforces the strategic bearish read.

catalysts.event: Singapore August CPI and MAS Consumer Price Developments
catalysts.rationale: The most consequential quote-leg release in the tactical window and the mechanism by which the market's view of the next MAS decision converges or diverges. July core rose to 2.0% from 1.6% on an 8.7% jump in electricity and gas as the Q3 regulated tariff passed through; August has a full month of that tariff rather than a partial one. A core reading at or above 2.2% makes a further band steepening the base case rather than a coin flip.

This is where the AI capital-expenditure deceleration is most visible: semiconductor output growth fell from 37.0% in May to 20.8% in June to 8.0% in July. A further leg toward zero would undercut the growth forecast underpinning the band-steepening case, which is bullish USD/SGD, and MAS's Managing Director names AI-boom sustainability as one of his two principal risks.

catalysts.event: US September quarter-end dollar funding date
catalysts.rationale: The first quarter-end since reserve balances resumed falling, at $2.92tn and drifting toward the roughly $3tn comfortable minimum, with the reverse repo facility drained to $702 million and no buffer left to absorb balance-sheet management. Because Singapore is a major Asian dollar centre whose banks run large dollar books, funding pressure transmits to the quote leg harder than to most, so any move from a +0.05bp basis lifts this pair.

catalysts.event: MAS October Monetary Policy Statement, Macroeconomic Review and Q3 advance GDP estimate — NOT IN THE GATED CALENDAR
catalysts.rationale: The single most important quote-leg event and the strategic inflection point, but it must be flagged: the supplied scheduled-decisions block contains no SGD entry at all, so this date is inherited from the quote dossier and is unverified rather than gated. Each MAS review can change the slope of the policy band, its width, or the level at which it is centred. The quote dossier assigns 55% to a further slight steepening toward about 1.50% a year against a published sell-side view closer to 35-40%; a steepening resets the band and the pair 60 to 90 pips lower, a hold unwinds the estimated 1.7% band deviation and lifts it 80 to 120 pips.

catalysts.event: Federal Reserve FOMC decision, no Summary of Economic Projections (gated)
catalysts.rationale: The first gated decision after September with no dot plot attached, which makes it the meeting at which the market must judge on the Committee's silence whether the September move was terminal. Under meeting-by-meeting data dependence this is a genuine repricing event rather than a formality, and for this pair it determines whether the dollar's 222bp advantage is a plateau or a step on a path. A pause with cycle-complete language is the most likely route to a lower USD/SGD.

catalysts.event: US-China tariff truce expiry, with China's reciprocal truce on 2026-11-19
catalysts.rationale: Singapore sends 22.0% of its goods exports to Greater China and 9.6% to the United States, so a lapse hits both ends of its entrepôt function simultaneously, and total merchandise trade running at +38.6% year on year is the flow that gets disrupted. The pair rises on this because the quote leg's real economy is the exposed one while the base currency benefits from the resulting risk-off through the dollar smile — the quote leg's haven status works against Asian peers, not against the dollar.

catalysts.event: Federal Reserve FOMC decision with Summary of Economic Projections (gated)
catalysts.rationale: The final gated Fed event in the strategic window and the release at which the 2027 median dot — currently 3.6%, implying a cut back from a September hike — is either confirmed or removed. Confirmation validates the strategic Bearish reading by making the dollar's advantage terminal; removal converts the September move into a cycle, widens the money-market gap toward 272bp or more, and would be the trigger to reverse the strategic stance.

catalysts.event: US year-end dollar funding turn and expiry of the tariff-exclusion process
catalysts.rationale: The direct analogue of December 2025, when SOFR-to-IORB spreads reached their widest since 2020 and standing repo usage spiked to a record $74.6bn on 31 December before collapsing to zero in January. Every precondition is in place and several are worse, with reserves draining about $20bn a week and no reverse repo buffer, and the 11 December funding cliff sits just before it. Tighter dollar funding pushes the base currency to the stress side of the smile and hits the quote leg through its dollar-clearing role.

invalidators.condition: USD/SGD closes above 1.28840 on a weekly basis — the top of the five-touch resistance zone that contains all three daily moving averages
invalidators.new_stance: Strategic stance moves from Bearish to Neutral
invalidators.mechanism: A weekly close there means spot has rejoined a still-bullishly-stacked moving-average configuration rather than diverging from it, converting systematic flow from absent to supportive of the base currency and putting the 52-week high at 1.30964 back in play. In pair terms it would say the S$NEER band's appreciation is being overwhelmed by the dollar leg rather than merely offset.

invalidators.condition: USD/SGD closes below 1.25883 on a weekly basis — the 52-week intraday low and the loose proxy for the inferred strong edge of the S$NEER band
invalidators.new_stance: Tactical stance moves from Bullish to Bearish
invalidators.mechanism: For this specific pair a break of that level is not a technical event but a policy inference: it would say the band's parameters have shifted rather than that the dollar is soft, and no four-week carry argument survives a re-parameterisation.

invalidators.condition: The FOMC holds the target range at 3.50-3.75% on 16 September rather than hiking
invalidators.new_stance: Tactical stance moves from Bullish to Bearish
invalidators.mechanism: Factor 1 supplies 63% of the tactical gross positive and its entire tactical case rests on a widening money-market gap that a hold would deny — while the quote leg, having no decision in the window, would face no offsetting dovish surprise of its own. A hold leaves the differential at 222bp against a band that continues to appreciate mechanically at roughly 10bp a month, so the pair falls on both legs at once.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: FOMC statement and implementation note; futures-implied probability in the preceding fortnight

invalidators.condition: MAS leaves the S$NEER slope, width and centre unchanged at its October review with no hawkish language about January
invalidators.new_stance: Strategic stance moves from Bearish to Neutral
invalidators.mechanism: The strategic case rests on a band that compounds at 60 to 75bp of trade-weighted appreciation over the window against a US path the Fed's own dots make terminal. A hold converts the estimated 1.7% band deviation from a policy-supported position into a reversion toward the midpoint, worth roughly 1.5% on the trade-weighted index and materially less on this pair, but enough to erase the base case.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: MAS October Monetary Policy Statement text
invalidators.monitor_frequency: once, mid-October (date unverified — not in the gated calendar)

invalidators.condition: The three-month EUR/USD cross-currency basis moves beyond -25bp for three consecutive sessions
invalidators.new_stance: Both tactical and strategic stances move toward Bullish
invalidators.mechanism: This invalidates the character of the thesis rather than its direction. A genuine dollar funding premium moves the base currency from the exceptionalism side of the smile to the stress side, and Singapore's role as an Asian dollar-clearing centre makes the quote leg a high-beta recipient — the pair would rise for reasons unrelated to the 222bp differential, and the rates-based framework in Factors 1, 2 and 6 would stop being the right lens.

invalidators.condition: The Fed delivers a second 25bp hike into the 9 December meeting, taking the target range to 4.00-4.25% and the money-market gap toward 272bp
invalidators.new_stance: Strategic stance moves from Bearish to Bullish
invalidators.mechanism: A differential widening past roughly 297bp overwhelms a 1.25-1.50% band slope in the primary pair even while the Singapore dollar continues appreciating on a trade-weighted basis. This is the cleanest single reversal condition in the report and it is dated.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: FOMC decisions on 28 October and 9 December and the accompanying Summary of Economic Projections

invalidators.condition: Singapore semiconductor manufacturing output growth turns negative year on year in any month
invalidators.new_stance: Strategic stance moves from Bearish to Neutral
invalidators.mechanism: The 4.5-5.5% growth forecast that underpins the widening output gap — and therefore the band-steepening case — is almost entirely an AI capital-expenditure story. Growth has already fallen from +37.0% in May to +8.0% in July, and MAS's Managing Director has explicitly named that boom's sustainability as one of his two principal risks. A collapsing quote-leg growth engine removes the reason for the appreciation the forward curve has already priced.

assumptions: Price series actually delivered: the payload supplied 130 data points covering 2026-03-06 to 2026-09-03, with spot 1.26714 at spotDate 2026-09-03. Moving averages, zones, the 52-week range and the 200-week figures are computed over the whole stored history (2007-12-21 to 2026-09-03, 4,880 weekday bars), not over the 130 bars shown. The payload's dataQuality array flags only 8 resistance / 0 support zones met the 2-touch threshold.

Spot date versus valuation date: the valuation date is 2026-09-01; spotDate is 2026-09-03, two trading sessions later, and the quote dossier's own reference close was 1.27117 on 2026-08-31. Every level, target, pip calculation and distance-to-average in this report is anchored to 1.26714, the payload spot; no fresher web quote has been substituted, and the 40-pip gap is disclosed rather than reconciled.

Moving-average basis: all averages are simple averages of trading-day closes, with weekend bars dropped on ingest (weekendBarsDropped: 0 for the delivered window). The 200-week average of 1.32176 with slope -0.000669/week is treated as a first-class structural level; convergence timing (~82 weeks at current slope) is outside both horizons.

Zone methodology and its shortfall: zones are computed by clustering weekly and monthly swing closes with touch counts; distances are measured from spot to zone midpoint. Detection returned eight resistance zones and zero support zones at the two-touch threshold. The support structure is therefore built from the payload's 52-week extremes, the lower boundary of the one zone in contact with price, and psychological round numbers (1.2600, 1.2500), which carry no touch counts. No web-sourced support/resistance level has been adopted into the levels list.

Volatility and options: implied volatility, the one-year IV percentile, the variance risk premium, the volatility term structure and the 25-delta risk reversal are null and permanently so, because no listed USD/SGD option exists on any exchange. No estimate has been substituted. carry_to_vol_ratio is consequently null; a realised-volatility ratio of approximately +0.73 is mentioned once and explicitly labelled as a different, non-comparable statistic.

The 222bp figure is a money-market spread, not a policy differential, because Singapore has no policy interest rate by construction — MAS targets the S$NEER band. The payload's policyDifferential and yield10yDifferential fields are both null for exactly that reason. Every reference to 222.2bp is US federal funds midpoint 3.625% minus SORA 1.4028%.

Yield vintages: the payload's US 10-year of 4.47% is a monthly observation as of 2026-06-01 and is not quoted as a live level; where a current US long yield is needed, the base dossier's 4.73% (2026-08-28) is used with the ~26bp vintage gap stated. SGS yields of 2.42% (10y) and 1.74% (2y) rest on a single source in the quote dossier and are carried as best available.

S$NEER band parameters are undisclosed: the estimated appreciation slope (~1.25%/yr), the estimated deviation (~1.7% above midpoint), and the conventional 2% half-width assumption are analyst reconstructions inherited from the quote dossier, whose publisher pages returned empty bodies on re-verification. They are best available and flagged; confidence is set below 50 wherever they are load-bearing (Factor 4, strategic path expectation).

No SGD schedule was supplied in the gated calendar: the scheduled-decisions block contains three FOMC dates and explicitly no SGD entry. The mid-October MAS review referenced throughout as the strategic inflection point is dossier-sourced and unverified, not gated, though the general quarterly cadence (January, April, July, October) is independently confirmed.

Bilateral trade: the IMF DOTS block supplied is used directly in Factor 5 and has not been re-estimated. US-reported and Singapore-reported figures disagree (a normal feature of entrepôt trade statistics) and this is disclosed rather than resolved; either way the flow is close to balanced and too small to drive the pair. Bilateral investment flows, an order of magnitude more material, were researched separately and are cited.

Direction verdict handling: this is pass 2 of 2. The ten factor stances, confidences, evidence types, weights, weighted contributions, net scores, convictions and both rationales arrived settled from a first pass deliberately denied the price payload, and are carried through unchanged. No factor has been re-scored because the chart disagrees with it; disagreement with the settled tactical direction is stated explicitly in the tactical rationale rather than smuggled into a factor score.

Weight adjustments: four factors were adjusted, each within the ±0.05 limit, each with a stated bilateral reason, and both weight sets sum to exactly 1.00. The framework's usual reduction of Factor 10 for non-USD crosses was not applied, because this is a USD pair.
